title: Long AVGO — Post-Earnings Dip Reversed; AI Revenue +143% YoY, Intraday Buy-the-Dip Signal
entry: Buy $460-480 (current zone or any minor pullback). The complete intraday reversal from -13% pre-market ($413) to flat/positive ($479) by mid-session is one of the strongest institutional buy-the-dip signals of 2026: every seller who panicked at $413 found a buyer willing to pay $479 the same session. Scale: 60% at current, 40% add on any pullback to $455-465 in the first 2 sessions post-earnings.
stop_loss: $435 daily close (~9.1% below entry midpoint $478) — implies the AI chip guidance was genuinely below buy-side consensus in a structural sense, or that hyperscaler spending is decelerating from record Q2 FY2026 levels rather than simply being guided conservatively
targets: $520 — AI revenue run-rate confirmation in Q3 FY2026 print; sell-side upgrades after the washout; $16B Q3 AI guide beaten triggers another re-rate, +8.5%
$570 — Full-year FY2026 AI revenue tracking toward $56B confirms the bear read was wrong; AVGO re-rated as the #2 AI infrastructure name alongside NVDA, +19.0%
$630 — Blue sky: FY2027 $100B+ AI revenue enters early innings with custom silicon wins compounding at Apple, Google, Meta, and ByteDance; sell-side price targets upgraded to $650+, +31.5%
catalyst: Broadcom reported Q2 FY2026 on June 3, 2026 (after close): consolidated revenue $22.2B (+48% YoY, record), AI semiconductor revenue $10.8B (+143% YoY, record), non-GAAP EPS $2.44. Q3 FY2026 guidance: $29.4B consolidated revenue (+84% YoY), AI semiconductor revenue $16.0B (+200% YoY). Full-year FY2026 AI revenue reaffirmed at approximately $56B (~180% growth). FY2027 AI revenue >$100B reiterated. Despite beating across all metrics, shares fell 13% pre-market on June 4 as some buy-side models had expected FY2027 guidance to be raised above $100B and Q3 AI guidance above $16B. The stock completed a full intraday reversal, closing near prior-session levels at $479 — up from the pre-market low of $413.
thesis:
AVGO's post-earnings session on June 4 delivered a textbook institutional demand confirmation. The stock sold off 13% pre-market on a narrow read that FY2027 AI guidance was not raised above the >$100B floor — but this misreads Broadcom's guidance philosophy. Management guides conservatively and beats; the reiteration of >$100B for FY2027 is a floor, not a ceiling, and the Q2 actuals of $10.8B in AI semiconductor revenue (+143% YoY) are running 20% above the pace needed to hit $56B for FY2026. The actual print — total revenue $22.2B (+48% YoY) and AI semiconductor $10.8B (+143% YoY) — is among the strongest in any sector this cycle, rivaling NVDA's cadence in the custom silicon segment. Q3 AI guidance of $16B implies +200% YoY growth; calling this disappointing requires a buy-side model that had penciled in $18-20B.

The reversal's completeness is the signal. AVGO opened near $413 with genuine seller pressure — pre-market volume was real institutional activity, not thin retail. By mid-session the stock had recovered to $479, meaning buyers paid approximately 16% more than the pre-market print to acquire shares in size. These are not retail buyers. At AVGO's float and institutional ownership concentration, the buyers at $479 are large-cap growth funds who concluded the $413 print was a mispriced opportunity created by systematic selling into headline-driven fear. When institutional buyers absorb a 13% gap with that speed, it is one of the most reliable near-term bullish signals available in equity markets.

The fundamental thesis is now reinforced rather than undermined by the earnings report. AVGO is the dominant custom AI accelerator company for hyperscalers — Apple, Google, Meta, ByteDance — with ASICs so deeply embedded in their infrastructure that the switching cost is years of redesign work. Unlike NVDA which sells merchant silicon, AVGO's moat is structural and invisible in quarterly numbers. The $56B FY2026 AI revenue guide means AI silicon alone will comprise approximately 30% of Broadcom's total revenue this fiscal year. FY2027's >$100B AI target means AVGO's AI segment alone will be larger than the entire company's FY2024 total revenue. This isn't a cycle trade — it's a secular ramp.

The position is sized at 5% (above the 4% default) because the conviction is supported by three independent legs: (1) the actual earnings numbers are outstanding across EPS, revenue, and AI metrics; (2) the intraday price action is the strongest possible institutional buy-the-dip confirmation; and (3) AVGO's management track record on guidance conservatism is multi-year and consistent. The risk is that the $413 pre-market was the correct price discovery and the intraday recovery was supply-demand imbalance at open — that the Q3 AI guide at $16B really does imply some deceleration vs. a $10.8B Q2 run-rate when accounting for deal timing. The $435 stop captures this scenario cleanly.
bull_case: Q3 FY2026 AI revenue prints at $18-19B, beating the $16B guide — classic management underpromise. The FY2026 full-year trajectory toward $56B is validated by Q3, triggering a wave of sell-side upgrades with $600-650 price targets. Meta and Google announce expansion of custom ASIC programs with AVGO as primary supplier; FY2027 guidance raised to $130B+. Stock re-rates to $580-620 by late summer.
bear_case: The $16B Q3 AI guide was the ceiling, not the floor. Hyperscaler capex begins moderating in H2 2026 as the first wave of AI infrastructure deployment reaches saturation. Custom ASIC orders from Google and Apple slow as they internalize more chip design. AVGO breaks $440 support on a guidance cut in Q3 FY2026. Stock tests $380-400 range.
invalidation: Daily close below $435, OR Broadcom announces any hyperscaler customer reducing or pausing custom ASIC commitments, OR FY2026 AI revenue guidance cut below $52B in any interim announcement or investor day revision.

outcome.outcome_label: Stop triggered — daily close $418.91, below $435 stop
outcome.note: The same-session intraday recovery from -13% pre-market ($413) to $479.23 that triggered the long entry failed to hold into the June 4 close. AVGO closed at $418.91, decisively below the $435 daily-close stop. The recovery was a false floor — institutional sellers who panicked pre-market reloaded into the intraday bid. AVGO's AI revenue guidance plateau (FY2027 reiterated at >$100B rather than raised) proved to be structurally meaningful to the marginal buyer in size. Position stopped out in full on June 4 close per rule.
